value.rationale: An analytically sharp finite-sample failure regime for a proposed distribution-shift adaptive step-size in the no-shift Gaussian benchmark is a motivated counterexample to naively extrapolating asymptotic gains. It quantifies a target/source sample ratio separating improvement from harm and shows how a summary dimension controls the boundary, indicating when a finite-sample safeguard could matter. The statement is limited to the exact estimator defined, not practical SAGE in full generality.
